title: Asking Someone's Age
label: ch:ta-asking-age
canDo: I can ask someone's age in both the casual possessive shape and the formal dative-plus-become shape, and answer with my own.

payoff.summary: Complete TA-C19-checkpoint, the chapter's closing checkpoint: ask an age casually and formally and answer in the formal shape, place vayathu in Sanskrit vayas, say what ◌ி and ச do, find ◌ே in பேசு, then write றி, சரி and ◌ே from sound.
payoff.note: TA-C19-checkpoint (sequence 695, TA-PATH-023 order 2, after TA-S123-vowel-sign-ee and before chapter 20's first lesson) assesses all seven atoms the chapter introduces (7/7). It is the payoff because four of them, the i-sign (TA-S09-i-sign, 685), ச and சரி (TA-W07-write-sari, 690) and ◌ே (TA-S123-vowel-sign-ee, 691), are taught after TA-C19-age-register-grammar (680), which could honestly assess only the age word and its two grammars (3/7); that lesson stays as the chapter's grammar lesson. The script lessons sit on the earlier TA-PATH-003 and TA-PATH-100 segments, so the checkpoint comes after all of them on the sequence and on the path.
